title: Seventy-two hours
logline: Thursday. The decision. 'One week. A scorched-earth parody.' The strip draws the sprint's clock: 72 hours as a circle he draws on the wall and starts crossing off. Barnaby goes to sleep for the duration.

panels.composition: The garage. WOOD drawing a circle on the wall in marker — a clock face — and writing 72 in it. BARNABY.

characters.pose: drawing a clock on the wall

balloons.text: One week. One. A scorched-earth parody of every idiot on that board. Then back to the ridge.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a man drawing a clock face with a marker on a garage wall and writing a number in it, a small dog watching, monitor glow

panels.composition: Bristol board. A stick figure. Four lines for a rotor on its head. Crude on purpose. His hand shaking with the effort of being bad.
props: a stick figure with a rotor

panels.composition: The dog, in the bed, one eye on the wall clock, going to sleep. The 72 crossed to 71. The CRT. The noodles. Night.

characters.pose: one eye open, going to sleep
